subject: Accounting
title: The Skimming Scheme
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Skimming Scheme.

hook.text: Cash comes in from a customer. Before it's recorded, an employee pockets it. The books never know.

buildup.text: Skimming is stealing cash before it enters the accounting system—making it nearly invisible.

discovery.text: Because the money was never recorded, traditional audits can't find it through book analysis alone.

twist.text: Detection requires comparing external data—bank deposits vs. register tapes, or customer confirmations.

climax.text: Surveillance cameras, surprise cash counts, and job rotation are the best prevention tools.

punchline.text: What never hits the books is hardest to find.

quiz.question: Why is skimming hard to detect through normal auditing?
options: The stolen cash is never recorded in the books
It only happens in cash-free businesses

details.summary: Skimming is a fraud scheme where cash is stolen before it's recorded in the accounting system—making it one of the hardest frauds to detect. This topic explains how skimming works at the register, in the mail room, and at the point of sale.
details.whyItMatters: Because skimmed cash is never recorded, the books appear balanced even while theft is occurring. Traditional reconciliation won't catch it—only behavioral and analytical detection methods work.
takeaways: Skimming steals cash before it enters the accounting records, so the books still balance
Common methods include pocketing cash sales without recording them and stealing incoming customer payments
Detection relies on trend analysis—unusual declines in cash-to-noncash sales ratios or receivable collection rates

faq.question: How does a skimming scheme work?
faq.answer: An employee intercepts cash before it's recorded in the accounting system—pocketing a cash sale without ringing it up, or stealing a customer's cash payment and not applying it to their account. Since the transaction is never recorded, the books still balance perfectly.

faq.question: How can organizations detect skimming?
faq.answer: Monitor trends: declining cash sales ratios when cash customers haven't changed, customer complaints about unpaid balances, shrinking inventory not matched by recorded sales, revenue per employee below benchmarks, and video surveillance at cash handling points.
